note: Both sets correctly capture the filter type (recursive, single-pole), the 0.25 Hz/-3 dB corner frequency, the 0.0125 s time step, and the endpoint Bode values (0 dB/0° at 0.01 Hz, about -12 dB/-75° at 1.00 Hz). Set A is the cleaner extraction: it adds defensible range/trend statements and only two misread values (-80° and -12.5 dB at 1.00 Hz, both contradicting its own quotes). Set B repeats the same chart points up to three times with conflicting values (-75°, -72°, -80° at 1.00 Hz) and supports several numeric claims with only the figure caption, which contains no values. Both sets omit the discrete-time state-space matrices (A_d=α, B_d=1-α, C_d=α, D_d=1-α) given in the text.
remarks: Both extractions read numeric points off the Bode plot curves, which are only approximately legible; values like -12 dB and -75° at 1.00 Hz are consistent with the plotted curves and the axis labels, but exact readings are not stated in the text. The recurring pattern in both sets is emitting several near-duplicate claims for the same (frequency, quantity) point with slightly different values (-12 vs -12.5 dB; -75 vs -72 vs -80 deg), i.e. chart-reading jitter treated as separate claims. Set B frequently uses the figure caption alone as the quote for numeric claims, which does not support the value. Important facts both sets miss: the state-space matrices A_d=α, B_d=1-α, C_d=α, D_d=1-α and the relation that the corner frequency is roughly one-quarter of the blade's first edgewise natural frequency (the latter is only implicit in the shared corner-frequency quote).
